days.title: Day 1
days.body:
Devotion
Peace doesn't begin when everything around you is finally in order. It begins when your heart finds its place in God.

We often think that if we could fix a particular problem, receive a particular answer, achieve a certain goal, or get clarity about our future, then we would finally have peace. But God invites us to experience peace even before those things happen.

The peace of God is not dependent on your circumstances becoming perfect. It comes from knowing that your life is held by a perfect God.

When your mind is fixed on your problems, your problems become bigger. When your mind is fixed on God, you begin to remember who is bigger than your problems.

Today, don't try to figure everything out. Come before God, slow down, and allow your heart to rest in Him.

Reflect:
- What has been occupying my mind more than God lately?
- Am I trusting God, or am I trying to control everything myself?
Prayer:

Lord, bring my heart back to You. Teach me to trust You even when I don't understand what is happening around me. Help me to stop carrying things that I have already placed in Your hands. Fix my mind upon You, and let Your presence become the place where my heart finds rest. Amen.

days.title: Day 2
days.body:
Devotion
Jesus never promised that we would have a life without trouble. But He promised us something greater than the absence of trouble — His presence in the middle of it.

The world offers peace when everything is going well. When finances are stable, relationships are good, plans are working, and the future looks certain. But the peace Jesus gives is different. His peace can remain even when life is uncertain.

You don't have to carry tomorrow today. You don't have to have every answer before you can rest. You don't have to pretend you're strong when you feel tired.

Jesus knows what troubles your heart. He knows the things you haven't told anyone. And He invites you to trust Him.

Let today be a reminder that peace is not something you have to manufacture. It is something you receive from Christ.

Reflect:
- What am I carrying today that Jesus is asking me to surrender?
- Am I looking for peace in circumstances, or in Christ?
Prayer:

Lord Jesus, thank You for the peace You give, a peace that the world cannot offer. I surrender my worries, my uncertainties, my fears, and the things I cannot control. Teach me to rest in Your promises and not be troubled by what I cannot see. Amen.

days.title: Day 3
days.body:
Devotion
Sometimes the reason we struggle to experience peace is because we never stop.

We are always thinking, planning, worrying, scrolling, working, expecting, or trying to solve something. Even when our bodies are resting, our minds are running.

But God says, Be still.

Stillness is not giving up. Stillness is not laziness. Stillness is an act of faith. It is the moment you stop trying to be in control of everything and acknowledge that God is God, and you are not.

You may not know what tomorrow holds. You may not know how a situation will turn out. But you can know the One who holds tomorrow.

Today, make space for silence. Read the Word slowly. Don't rush through the chapters just to finish them. Sit with a verse. Let God speak before you speak, and let His presence settle your heart.

Reflect:
- When was the last time I was genuinely still before God?
- What would it look like for me to trust God without constantly trying to figure everything out?
Prayer:

Father, quiet my mind. Help me to stop being consumed by the things around me. Teach me the beauty of being still in Your presence. When my thoughts become loud, remind me that You are God, You are in control, and You are faithful. Amen.

days.title: Day 4
days.body:
Devotion
Sometimes our lack of peace comes from fear — fear of losing something, fear of failing, fear of the unknown, fear that things will not work out, or even fear that God is somehow distant from us.

But Romans 8 reminds us of a truth that we must never forget: we are loved by God, and nothing can separate us from that love in Christ.

You may go through difficult seasons. You may have days when you don't feel spiritually strong. You may not always understand what God is doing. But His love is not changing according to your feelings, your circumstances, or your performance.

You don't have to earn God's love today. You don't have to prove yourself to Him. You can come to Him as you are.

When you know you are secure in God's love, you don't have to live in constant fear. You can face the unknown with confidence, not because you know what will happen, but because you know who holds you.

Reflect:
- Do I believe God's love for me remains even when I feel weak?
- What fear do I need to bring before Him today?
Prayer:

Father, thank You that Your love for me is not dependent on my strength or circumstances. Help me to live with the assurance that I belong to You. When fear comes, remind me of Your Word. Give me confidence to walk forward knowing that nothing can separate me from Your love. Amen.

days.title: Day 5
days.body:
Devotion
There is a difference between carrying something and surrendering something.

You can pray about a situation and still continue carrying it in your mind. You can say that you trust God, yet spend every day worrying about how things will turn out. Surrender means bringing it before God and trusting Him even when you don't have the ability to change the outcome.

God doesn't ask you to carry every burden by yourself. He invites you to bring it to Him because He cares for you.

Not just the big things. The little things too. Your disappointments, your unanswered prayers, your future, your family, your responsibilities, your thoughts, and the things that quietly trouble you.

As you conclude these five days, don't just leave with a feeling of peace. Leave with a decision to trust God daily.

Peace is not a one-time experience. It is a daily surrender.

Reflect:
- What am I still holding on to that I need to surrender to God?
- Can I trust God even if He doesn't answer in the way or timing I expect?
Prayer:

Father, I bring everything before You. Every burden, every concern, every fear, every unanswered question. I surrender what I cannot control and trust You with what I cannot understand. Thank You for caring for me. Help me to walk in Your peace, not only today, but every day. Let my heart rest in You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
